skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2, at the very start, the interviewer said the Committee and company are the clients, not the witness, and that counsel cannot give the witness legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and disclose what is learned without the witness's consent. T4 and T5 confirm the witness understood.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 sets out how the interview will proceed, asks for complete answers, and asks the witness to flag speculation and say whether they remember or are reconstructing.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asks the witness to restate who is represented and who controls privilege, and T5 shows the warning was understood before questions began.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T356 asks for anything to add, and covers confidentiality, keeping documents, and not speaking with other witnesses. The next steps are only a vague 'We may follow up'.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
Before we go on, could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
The witness restated that the company represents the Committee, not the witness, and that the company controls the privilege and can share what the witness says.
Please give me complete answers, even if a detail seems minor.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as T16, T32, T44 and T80 let the witness walk through events, but some topics were left after short answers.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The order runs from background to LJM1, the Rhythms unwind, Chewco, the controls, and then personal interests, which is sensible. The Southampton document came late, after the witness had already been asked about the Foundation.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are clear and single. A few, such as T168, restate several points at once.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stayed calm and neutral when the witness deflected, for example at T306 and T150, and kept control of the interview throughout.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer moved from T122 to the specific Foundation question at T124 and followed the witness's estimates at T114 to T119. Some topics, such as the Causey group reviewers at T41 to T43, were not pursued further.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about the controls put in place when the Board approved LJM2 in October 1999.
The interview moved in a sensible order from the witness's role (T8) to Global Finance and Kopper (T10 to T15) and then to LJM1 (T16).
The Foundation received about $4.5 million from an interest tied to the Rhythms unwind. Help me understand how those fit together.
Did your family, or any entity connected with you, have one?
What investments connected to LJM1 did the foundation make in early 2000?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed up on evasive and inconsistent answers, including T56, T144, T252, T306 and T332. The witness's 'I don't believe it came up' answers were tested.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The who, what, when and how were covered for the Raptor I closing and approval sheets (T98 to T102) and for the Chewco buyout. Some details, such as the exact Board disclosure, were not fully pinned down.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The interviewer used notes (T62), minutes (T70), the Southampton agreement (T128) and the handwritten note (T300) to refresh memory. Other retrieval approaches were not tried for the names of the Causey group.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer separated first-hand knowledge from hearsay, for example at T56 and T346 ('did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?').

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: At T336, T338, T340, T342 and T344 the interviewer asked who else to speak with, including Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, McMahon and Skilling.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked for account statements (T350), the deal files (T349) and personal notes and emails (T352), and asked what the witness's personal records cover (T354).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked how certain the witness was about the $4.5 million figure (T144), asked for a best estimate (T118), and tested confidence in the $229 million figure (T222).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers were followed up, such as 'A few million' at T141, the Foundation's return at T142, and the payment approval after counsel's advice in T312 to T333.

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
The minutes record you saying there had been "tremendous utilization" of Raptor I. Our information is that Talon hadn't yet done any derivatives with Enron. Help me understand how those fit together.
Earlier you told me you stayed out of the Chewco buyout. This note, addressed to "Andy," refers to $10.5 million for the buyout. Help me understand how those fit together.
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
How do you know that: did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
How certain are you of that figure?
What's your best estimate?
Our information is that on May 1, 2000, about six weeks after it invested, the Foundation received roughly $4.5 million on its $25,000. Is that accurate?
Do you have any personal files, notes, or emails about LJM, Chewco, or Southampton?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
Turning to the Raptor returns. Tell me what you remember about the return the Board and Finance Committee expected LJM2 to earn on the Raptors.
What returns did LJM2 actually earn on the Raptors?
I'd like to show you LJM2's October 2000 report to its investors. Do you recognize it?
I'm not suggesting you wrote it. Do you recognize it?
It says their return "was not at risk" because LJM2 "had already received its return of and on capital." Is that what you told them?
Did you consider whether the Board should know that LJM2's returns were several times what it had been told?
The structure needed outside investors' money to stay at risk. Help me understand how a return that "was not at risk" fits with that.

missed_opportunities: T355: When the witness offered personal notes and emails kept at home and on a personal account, the interviewer asked what they cover but did not ask for immediate preservation of those specific sources. The only preservation instruction came in the generic closing at T356.
tips: Before you move to the next topic, what exact document or record shows what the Board or Finance Committee received about LJM2's returns, and can you name the person who sent it?

Since your personal notes and emails are at home and on a personal account, can you confirm today that you will keep those specific sources intact, and what would you need to do to make sure nothing is deleted?
